periods.summary: Wallenshtein confronts Or-Gaule when the latter attacks Rebellion headquarters. He denounces Or-Gaule's empty malice and reveals his friction-manipulating sword ability, which hard-counters Or-Gaule's threads by preventing physical contact and binding the threads through extreme friction. He cuts away the mountain roof with Mountain-Splitting Slash, disables Or-Gaule's footing, and nearly executes him. Or-Gaule, however, had never intended a fair duel; Naseem Salim ambushes Wallenshtein, pierces his chest, and drains his body dry. Wallenshtein dies before learning that the Tyrant is not actually in the headquarters.

key_events.summary: Overpowers Or-Gaule through ability compatibility but is killed by Naseem's ambush.

relationships.or-gaule: Discovers the child's puppet crimes, names him a born evil, and gives him the ultimatum that leads to Bloody Cross.

periods.summary: In Or-Gaule's puppet-play retelling of his childhood, Wallenstein finds young Orles Gaul under a bridge after investigating unnatural outbreaks of violence in nearby towns. He identifies Orles's puppet ability and says it could serve Rebellion. When Orles resists and tries to control him, Wallenstein's ability prevents the threads from making meaningful contact. He nearly crushes Orles against a bridge pillar and then changes tactics, giving him one week: if Orles is the only living person in the village when Wallenstein returns, Wallenstein will take him to Rebellion; otherwise he will kill everyone, including Orles. He tells the child to consider whether Wallenstein or the villagers are truly trying to kill him, planting the resentment that leads Orles to massacre the village during his birthday celebration.

key_events.summary: Forces young Orles Gaul to choose between normal society and becoming Rebellion's evil.
